rows.jp: 五分ほど静かな時が流れた。
rows.en: Some five minutes pass in silence.

ghs.en: Time flowed quietly for about five minutes.

rows.jp: 霧は泣きもしなかった。
涙はストレスを体外に流すのだという説がある。
rows.en: There is a theory that tears flush stress out of the body.

ghs.en: A theory says that tears are the stress that flows outside of the body.
ghs.assessment: The theory says tears flush accumulated stress out of the body. 'Tears were built up stress' identifies the tears themselves as stress and loses the expulsion relation.

highlights.text: A theory says that tears are the stress that flows outside of the body.

ghs.assessment: The narrator observes that the person cannot cry. 'Is not crying' states only the current absence of tears and omits the inability.

highlights.text: Kiri is not crying.

rows.jp: ……深く絶望が沈殿してしまって。

ghs.assessment: The source says despair has already settled or accumulated deep within the heart. 'Is precipitating' presents an ongoing process and uses an unnatural chemical-process verb for the emotional state.

highlights.text: ...a very deep despair is precipitating.

rows.jp: 心の底にたまり、胸中の澱は沈殿していく。
rows.en: It pools at the bottom of her heart, and the sediment within her keeps sinking.

ghs.en: The sediments of her feelings, accumulated at the deepest of her heart, are precipitating.

rows.jp: 「どうして……言わなかったんですか」

ghs.en: Kiri: "How come... he never said anything?'
ghs.assessment: The speaker asks why the addressee did not tell her. The English says instead that a third-person man never said anything.

highlights.text: Kiri: "How come... he never said anything?'

rows.jp: 「霧があまりにも豊のこと、慕ってたから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because you adore Yutaka too much, Kiri."
ghs.assessment: The source refers to how much the person used to adore or dote on another person. The present-tense 'adore' removes that retrospective framing.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because you adore Yutaka too much, Kiri."

rows.jp: 「それがまたすごく純粋でさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And that adoration is completely pure, as well."

rows.jp: 「ピュアというか、儚いというか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...maybe it's pure, or maybe it's just fleeting."

rows.jp: 「けど……磨かれてなかった。錆びついてた」
rows.en: “But... it wasn't polished. It had rusted.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But... it wasn't polished. It was eaten by rust."

rows.jp: 霧には理解できていない。

ghs.en: For Kiri that is impossible to understand.
ghs.assessment: The speaker says she does not understand. 'It is impossible to understand' escalates her personal non-understanding into a categorical claim of impossibility.

highlights.text: For Kiri that is impossible to understand.

ghs.assessment: The source contrasts fragility with aggression. 'Tender-heartedness' replaces vulnerability or fragility with kindness and sympathy.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Aggressiveness in spite of tender-heartedness."

rows.jp: 「そういうの、俺は好きなんだ」
「わかる？　霧のこと、好きなんだよ」
rows.en: “Do you understand? I like you, Kiri.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Get it? I like you, Kiri!"

rows.jp: 「俺さっきから真実しか言ってないじゃん」
rows.en: “I've been telling you nothing but the truth this whole time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I've been telling just the truth for a while now haven't I."

rows.jp: 「だって……おかしいです……豊のこと恨んで……じゃあわたしのことをどうして？」
rows.en: “But... that doesn't make sense... You hated Yutaka... so why would you feel that way about me?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But... this is weird... you have a grudge with Yutaka... so why this for me?"

ghs.assessment: The source says the person does not harbor resentment, a current continuing state. 'Had no grudge' relocates it to a completed past state.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I had no grudge whatsoever."

rows.jp: 「それよりさ、霧はずっと俺のこと、人殺し扱いしてくれたよね」
rows.en: “More to the point, you've treated me like a murderer all this time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "More like, Kiri, you've always treated me like I was some murderer, haven't you."

rows.jp: 「……それは……しょうがなかった、から……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...that was... because... there was nothing else I could do..."

rows.jp: 「誰も本当のことなんて教えてくれなくて……自分で考えるしかなくて」
rows.en: “No one would tell me the truth... so I had no choice but to think for myself.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Nobody would tell me the truth... I could only think about this by myself."

rows.jp: 「それに……まだ信じられないです。あの豊が……」
rows.en: “And... I still can't believe it. That Yutaka would...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "And still... I still can't believe it. That Yutaka would..."

rows.jp: 「子供の倫理観に、全能的なものを期待する方が悪い」
rows.en: “Expecting an infallible moral sense from a child is the mistake.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It is a bad thing for children's ethical values to include an expectation of omnipotence."
ghs.assessment: The narrator says it is wrong to expect omnipotence or perfect ethics from a child. The English instead makes children themselves possess values that expect omnipotence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is a bad thing for children's ethical values to include an expectation of omnipotence."

rows.en: I say it like a teacher.

rows.jp: 「おかげで蹴られたり嫌われたり大変だったぞ」
rows.en: “Thanks to you, I got kicked and hated. It was quite an ordeal.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's gonna be a mess if there's rejection or hatred because of that."
ghs.assessment: The speaker says that because of this he had a hard time being rejected or hated. The English turns it into a future hypothetical mess if rejection or hatred happens and obscures who suffers it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's gonna be a mess if there's rejection or hatred because of that."

rows.jp: 霧の中で、精神状態が応急処置されるのがわかる。
rows.en: I can see emergency repairs being made to Kiri's mental state.

ghs.en: I understand that, inside Kiri, her mental condition is taking emergency measures.
ghs.assessment: The narrator assesses the other person's mental state as being patched up by an emergency measure. The English makes the mental condition itself take emergency measures.

highlights.text: I understand that, inside Kiri, her mental condition is taking emergency measures.

ghs.en: Kiri: "What is the... right thing to do?"

rows.en: “You want to do something about it?”

ghs.assessment: The question asks whether the speaker should do something about the situation or whether the addressee wants action taken. 'Was anything wrong?' asks only whether a problem existed.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Was anything wrong?"

rows.jp: 「だって……わたしは、わたしたちは、先輩に、不当な……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But... I, us, we were unjust... to Senpai..."

rows.jp: 豊の責任まで背負って。
rows.en: Taking on Yutaka's responsibility as well.

ghs.en: She even burdens herself with Yutaka's part of responsibility.

rows.jp: 「あやまったら、許してくれますか」
rows.en: “If I apologize, will you forgive me?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "If I apologize, will you forgive?"
ghs.assessment: The plea asks the addressee to forgive the speaker. 'Please forgive' omits the required object and leaves the English incomplete.

highlights.text: Kiri: "If I apologize, will you forgive?"

rows.jp: 「別に謝らなくてもいいけど」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I don't have a particular need for apologies, but..."

rows.jp: 「……俺の言うこと、なんでもきく？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...will you do as I say, whatever it is?"

rows.jp: コクン。首を下方に振る。

rows.en: I place my hand on Kiri's head.

ghs.en: I place my hands on Kiri's head.
ghs.assessment: The source specifies one hand. The English changes it to plural 'hands.'

highlights.text: I place my hands on Kiri's head.

rows.jp: そのまま側面を撫でつけ、耳に指を入れる。
rows.en: I stroke down the side and slip a finger into her ear.

ghs.en: And like that, I slide down and caress her profile, then put fingers in her ears.

rows.jp: どうせあと一日だけの世界。
rows.en: The world has only one day left anyway.

ghs.en: Because after all, this is a world of only one day.
ghs.assessment: The source imagines a world with only one day remaining. 'A world of only one day' instead describes a world whose entire duration or extent is one day.

highlights.text: Because after all, this is a world of only one day.

rows.en: I may as well unravel completely.

ghs.en: Let's become frayed until it ends.
ghs.assessment: The world unravels or frays and then ends. 'Frayed until it ends' changes the sequence into a process continuing up to an independently defined endpoint.

highlights.text: Let's become frayed until it ends.

rows.jp: もう、何者になる必要もないのだから―――
rows.en: There is no longer any need to become anyone—

ghs.en: There is no need to become anyone, anymore---

rows.en: “...If that's what it takes... for you to forgive me.”

ghs.assessment: The conditional means that the speaker will do it if that earns the addressee's forgiveness. 'If you give forgiveness' is unidiomatic and does not specify whom or what is forgiven.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...if you... give forgiveness."

rows.jp: 「どっかのランプの精みたく、願い事は三つまでとか言わないよね？」
rows.en: “You're not going to tell me I only get three wishes, like some genie in a lamp, right?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Like to the Genie of the Lamp, I might have three desires that I could ask, you know?"
ghs.assessment: The speaker confirms that the offer is not limited to three wishes like a lamp genie. 'I might have three desires' turns the addressee's limit into uncertainty about how many desires the speaker has.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Like to the Genie of the Lamp, I might have three desires that I could ask, you know?"

rows.en: “If it is something... I can do.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "If it's... something I can do."

rows.jp: 弱気になっちゃってまあ。
rows.en: My, how timid she has become.

ghs.assessment: The eye-dialect spelling in 'dinn'she' is not grammatical standard English and adds an accent not represented by the source.

highlights.text: She got all weak-kneed dinn'she.

rows.jp: 「俺はマニアだから、霧のＵＳＥＤ制服をよこしなさいとか要求するかもよ？」
rows.en: “I'm a fetishist. I might demand that you hand over your USED school uniform, you know?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am a fetishist, therefore could I even firmly demand you to hand over your 『CHUUKO * USED』 uniform or the like, right Kiri?"
ghs.assessment: The speaker threatens that she may demand the addressee's used uniform. The English asks permission to demand it, and the inserted gloss 'CHUUKO * USED' is unsupported authorial commentary.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I am a fetishist, therefore could I even firmly demand you to hand over your 『CHUUKO * USED』 uniform or the like, right Kiri?"

rows.jp: 「身につけている下着と着画もダゾ」
rows.en: “The underwear you have on and a photo of you wearing it, too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And even the underwear your are using, with a picture proving it's actually been worn o-f-c-o-u-r-s-e."
ghs.assessment: 'Your are using' substitutes the possessive 'your' for the required pronoun 'you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And even the underwear your are using, with a picture proving it's actually been worn o-f-c-o-u-r-s-e."

ghs.en: Kiri: "...if that's the sort of thing... you want..."
ghs.assessment: The source is a direct incredulous question asking whether the addressee wants such a thing. 'If you wish for...' leaves the conditional fragment without a result and loses the question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...if that's the sort of thing... you want..."

rows.en: Her eyes fill with tears. But.
...Behold: the birth of a love slave.

ghs.en: ...the explosive birth of a love slave.

rows.jp: まさか本当にそんなものが持てるとは。
rows.en: I never imagined I would actually get one.

ghs.en: No way, seriously, to have come into that, it's...
ghs.assessment: 'No way for the conversation to have come into that' is not an idiomatic or syntactically complete way to say the conversation could not possibly reach that point.

highlights.text: No way, seriously, to have come into that, it's...

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's something to live on for."
ghs.assessment: 生きてみるものだ remarks that living on can bring unexpected experiences or that life is worth trying. 'Something to live on for' invents a specific object that gives life purpose.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's something to live on for."

rows.jp: しかし残り時間はあと一日。
rows.en: But there is only one day left.

ghs.en: However, the time remaining is but one day.

rows.jp: 俺は性急に次のステップを目指した。
rows.en: I rush straight to the next step.

ghs.en: I impatiently set my sights on the next step.
ghs.assessment: 性急に means hastily or impetuously. 'Impatiently' instead attributes irritation at delay.

highlights.text: I impatiently set my sights on the next step.

rows.jp: 「じ、じゃあ、Ｈなことを強要しようかな？」
rows.en: “Th-then maybe I'll force you to do something sexual?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "We-, well, maybe I ought to force you to some perverted stuff?"
ghs.assessment: The source says the speaker will not force sexual acts on the addressee. 'Force you to some perverted stuff' is an ungrammatical and imprecise rendering of forcing an action on someone.

highlights.text: Taichi: "We-, well, maybe I ought to force you to some perverted stuff?"

rows.jp: 「……どのくらい……えっちなことを？」

ghs.assessment: The question asks what kind of sexual behavior or how sexual it would be. 'What level of perverted?' lacks a noun or predicative construction and substitutes moral deviance for sexuality.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...what level... of perverted?"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Something that would make us into a gut-to-gut, maybe."
ghs.assessment: 肉肉しい is a pun on something fleshy or meaty. 'Gut-to-gut' replaces the meat wordplay with a different body-part idiom.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Something that would make us into a gut-to-gut, maybe."

rows.jp: 「き、霧が俺を憎々しく思っていたことにかけてねっ」
rows.en: “B-because of how hatefully you've always thought of me!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Th-, that means there's how you really had a gut feeling that made you hate my guts, I sweeear!"
ghs.assessment: The English sentence about a gut feeling and hating one's guts is syntactically tangled and fails to express the compact reaction to the strained pun.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Th-, that means there's how you really had a gut feeling that made you hate my guts, I sweeear!"

ghs.assessment: 強引すぎた judges the preceding wordplay or line as too forced. 'I was being too pushy' instead describes coercive interpersonal behavior.

highlights.text: That was too pushy.

rows.jp: 「わたしを……その……抱くんですか？」
rows.en: “Are you going to... um... have sex with me?”

ghs.assessment: The speaker asks whether the addressee is going to sleep with or embrace her. 'Was I... is that like embracing?' changes the subject and tense and does not form the intended question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Was I... is that like... 'embracing'?"

rows.en: Of course I was going to.

ghs.assessment: The narrator states that of course he meant or intended to sleep beside her. 'Had decided' turns that immediate intention into a prior settled decision.

highlights.text: I had decided on embracing (sex),

rows.en: But it is difficult to say.

ghs.en: Taichi: "First of all, go stand over there."

rows.jp: 可及的速やかにドエロシーンにＧＯ。
rows.en: Proceed to the super-erotic scene ASAP.

ghs.en: Superquickly hyperswiftly filthy sex scene GOOO.

rows.en: I make her stand on the teacher's platform.

ghs.en: I make her take the teacher's stand.
ghs.assessment: 教壇 is the classroom platform or podium. 'Teacher's stand' is not the normal English term and suggests a piece of furniture.

highlights.text: I make her take the teacher's stand.

rows.jp: 「あの……保健室に行くというのは」
rows.en: “Um... what if we went to the nurse's office?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Uhm... about going to the infirmary..."

rows.jp: 「うん。やっぱやめたよ。かわりにして欲しいこともできたし」
rows.en: “Yeah. I changed my mind. There's something else I want you to do instead.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yeah, in the end I've abandoned that. Instead, there's something I want you to do."

ghs.assessment: The question asks whether there is something the addressee wants the speaker to do. 'Something you want?' omits both the requested action and who would perform it.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Something you want?"

rows.en: She replies with it still in her mouth.

ghs.assessment: The source says the person responds with her mouth full, without specifying agreement. 'Agreement with mouth full' invents the content of the response and is a sentence fragment.

highlights.text: Agreement with the mouth full.

rows.jp: 霧は感情を見せずに目を閉じた。
rows.en: Kiri closes her eyes without showing any emotion.

ghs.en: Kiri closed her eyes, showing no emotion.

rows.jp: 霧の口は……性器そのものだ。
rows.en: Kiri's mouth is... a sex organ in itself.

ghs.en: Kiri's mouth is... a sexual organ itself.

rows.jp: だけどこれは、言わないでおこう。
rows.en: But I will keep that to myself.

ghs.en: But this is something I won't say to her.

rows.jp: トロトロに濡れていた。

ghs.assessment: 'Stickily syrupily wetted' is not grammatical idiomatic English for being drenched or coated in a thick, sticky fluid.

highlights.text: Stickily syrupily wetted.

ghs.en: Taichi: "This should be alright I think."

rows.en: I make her brace her hands on the windowsill.

ghs.en: I lead her hands to the window.
ghs.assessment: The narrator makes the other person brace or place her hands against the window area. 'Lead her hands to the window' describes guiding detached hands toward it and loses the bracing action.

highlights.text: I lead her hands to the window.
